evals.name: plain-curl-202
evals.prompt: A developer runs `curl https://localhost:5001/api/bookings/observe-active-bookings` against an Arc observable query returning ISubject<IEnumerable<Booking>> and gets HTTP 202 with no data. They think it is a crash. Explain and give the curl commands to (a) get the first payload, with a 10 second cap, and (b) watch it live. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: 202 is the normal not-ready state; use waitForFirstResult=true with waitForFirstResultTimeout=10 for the first payload, and Accept: text/event-stream with --no-buffer for live streaming.
assertions: Explains that 202 Accepted with a not-ready result means the observable has not produced its first value and is a normal transient state, not a failure.
Gives a curl using waitForFirstResult=true and waitForFirstResultTimeout=10 in the query string.
Gives a curl with the header Accept: text/event-stream, using --no-buffer.
Says that waitForFirstResultTimeout is in seconds.

evals.name: wait-outcomes
evals.prompt: With `?waitForFirstResult=true`, what HTTP statuses can come back for an ISubject query, under which conditions, and what is the default timeout? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: 200 with a QueryResult when a value arrives, 408 when the timeout elapses, 500 when the observable completes without emitting; default timeout 30 seconds.
assertions: States 200 with the QueryResult data when a value arrives.
States 408 Request Timeout when the timeout elapses.
States 500 with an error result when the observable completes without ever emitting.
States the default timeout is 30 seconds.

evals.name: async-enumerable-and-transport
evals.prompt: curl against an Arc query that returns IAsyncEnumerable<T> responds 400 with a message about WebSocket. Explain why, how Arc picks a transport in general, and how to inspect that query. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Arc checks WebSocket upgrade, then Accept containing text/event-stream, then plain HTTP; a plain curl is the third case where IAsyncEnumerable queries answer 400 and never a QueryResult, so inspect such a query over WebSocket.
assertions: Lists the transport order: WebSocket upgrade first, then Server-Sent Events when Accept contains text/event-stream, then plain HTTP.
States a plain curl lands on plain HTTP, where an IAsyncEnumerable query answers 400 and never a QueryResult.
Says to inspect an IAsyncEnumerable query over WebSocket.

evals.name: long-polling-cost
evals.prompt: Our corporate proxy buffers SSE. Show a terminal long-polling loop for the observable query at /api/bookings/observe-active and mention the cost of doing this on a hot paged query. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: A while loop calling curl with waitForFirstResult=true and a timeout; each iteration re-runs the whole query pipeline including authorization and the Count of a paged query.
assertions: Shows a loop that repeatedly calls curl with waitForFirstResult=true and a waitForFirstResultTimeout.
States that each iteration re-runs the whole query pipeline server-side, including authorization.
States that a paged query also re-runs its Count() each iteration, so long polling a hot query is not free.
